era_setting.place: Atlanta, Fulton County, Georgia, USA -- specifically 3756 Denville Trace SW and 3741 Landau Lane SW, three or four houses apart; with the Richard B. Russell Federal Building and the Elbert P. Tuttle Court of Appeals Building in downtown Atlanta, the Supreme Court of the United States in Washington, D.C., and one chapter in Collinsville, Illinois
era_setting.notes: READ THE SPLIT, NOT THE RANGE. 96% of this film is 2017-2026 and contemporary American stock is therefore the CORRECT dressing, not a compromise -- a 2020s suburban front door, a 2020s patrol light, a 2020s courthouse corridor are all in period. ACT_4 alone is April 1973 to 1974 (Collinsville, Illinois; the Senate Committee on Government Operations; the FTCA amendment), and NOTHING contemporary may appear in it: no mobile phone, no flat screen, no modern vehicle, no LED, no modern signage, no laptop, no bodycam. The archive shelf holds, channel-wide, nine archival clips whose title carries a 1955-1985 marker and not one of them is an American street, house, car or hearing room, so ACT_4 is dressed from commissioned plates and i2v, never from a footage query -- see approved_deviations entry 2. Conversely the contemporary 96% must NOT be dressed with archival newsreel: the same measurement returns Pearl Harbor and Dieppe for the word 'raid', and a WWII naval raid inside a 2017 Atlanta film is the EP62 greene failure repeated.

forbidden_claims: stating in the film's own voice that martin was held at gunpoint for approximately one hour, or that the agents were in the home for no more than five minutes, or that no agent touched martin. the record contains both accounts from opposite sides and they cannot both be true. every reference is attributed out loud -- 'the family swore' for the complaint's one hour, 'the court found' for the five minutes -- and the gap between them is stated as a gap

saying that agent guerra or the fbi lied, covered up, destroyed evidence, or threw the gps away in order to destroy evidence. the district court expressly declined to decide spoliation because the plaintiffs deferred it, and no tribunal has found it. the film may say exactly what the supreme court says -- that no one could confirm his account later because he threw the device away not long after the raid -- and stop there

saying that lawrence guerra was found liable, disciplined, suspended, fired, prosecuted, or found to have violated the fourth amendment. the opposite is on the record: qualified immunity, and an express finding that his actions did not violate the fourth amendment

saying that the family won, was paid, recovered damages, was compensated by the government, or received a settlement. as of 12 august 2026 they have recovered nothing under the federal tort claims act. the only payment anywhere in the record is a private insurer covering physical damage to the house, and that is counsel's account, not a court finding

saying the supreme court held that the family should win, that it found the fbi liable, or that it ruled for the family, without stating what it actually decided. it decided two legal questions, vacated the judgment, and expressly said the remaining questions about the discretionary-function exception lie well beyond the two questions it granted certiorari to address

saying the case is over, decided, resolved or finished, that the eleventh circuit has ruled, or predicting what it will do. it heard argument on remand on 25 march 2026 and on the record retrieved on 12 august 2026 no decision has issued

asserting in the film's own voice that this was a no-knock raid. the complaint pleads a no-knock warrant and the eleventh circuit's opinion uses that phrase, and the district court found that guerra knocked, announced, and that the team waited ten to twenty seconds before breaching. attribute, never assert
any address other than 3741 landau lane sw and 3756 denville trace sw. the institute for justice's own case page writes 3731 landau lane and that is an error

characterising joseph riley beyond what the opinions say -- that warrants were issued for his arrest and for the search of his home at 3741 landau lane, and that the fbi determined he posed a high risk of violence. never convicted, never 'the drug dealer' in the film's own voice, never depicted, never named in a title or thumbnail

any dollar figure attached to this case: what was claimed, what was demanded, what was offered at mediation, what the door cost, what the therapy cost. no sum certain was retrieved from any document. the absence may be stated; a number may not be invented

the child's surname, his age today, his school, his town, his current condition, any invented thought or dramatised moment beyond the four sentences his mother's complaint gives, and any image of a child anywhere in the film
any statement about whether curtrina martin and toi cliatt are still together, or any causal claim about their relationship
saying in the film's own voice that the fbi refused to pay. that is plaintiffs' counsel's characterisation. the united states litigated immunity; no refusal-to-pay document was retrieved

any count, rate or trend of wrong-house raids -- 'this happens x times a year', 'hundreds', 'thousands', 'it keeps happening' with a number attached. nothing retrieved supports a number. the pattern may be shown only through named cases: collinsville 1973, mesa v. united states 1997, and vivas v. united states 2021 as the district court cites it
any collinsville detail beyond the five sentences the sotomayor concurrence quotes, and any statement that all fifteen officers there were federal

saying that fbi body-camera or surveillance footage of the raid exists, or presenting the atlanta police department body-camera footage as footage of the raid itself. it shows officers staged outside the house, and counsel states there is none from the swat team

quoting 'the government said checking the address was optional' as if it were said. the government's actual position is that checking the house number at the end of the driveway means exposing the agents to potential lines of fire from the windows. the paraphrase may appear outside quotation marks and only beside the real words
saying the raid happened at 4 a.m. the complaint says approximately 4:00 to 4:30 a.m.; every court document and the warrant's own schedule say at or about 5:00 a.m. the film uses 5:00 a.m.

presenting any generated image as an authentic record: the warrant, the operation order, the swat addendum, a photograph of either house, the gps device, a page of the court file, a docket sheet, a newspaper front page, body-camera footage, or a likeness of curtrina martin, toi cliatt, the child, lawrence guerra, joseph riley, any agent, any judge, any justice or any attorney

attaching any political framing to this raid, this agency or these courts -- an administration, a party, a movement, a president's name, an election. the appointing presidents of the remand panel are on the public record and are deliberately not used

saying that congress passed the 1974 amendment because of wrong-house raids as the film's own assertion without attributing it to the senate report as quoted in the concurrence, and without also stating the majority's answer that legislative history is not the law

saying the fbi had no rules, no procedures or no training. the finding is narrower and must be quoted as it stands: no fbi policy or procedure dictates how to locate or navigate to the target, whether to use a gps device or what type, whether or how to conduct a site survey or drive-by, or how long to wait before entering after knocking and announcing

naming the wrong actor anywhere in a title, a thumbnail line, a description sentence, a chapter name or an on-screen card. this is a FEDERAL case about an FBI raid: the raiding party was a six-member FBI SWAT team led by an FBI special agent, accompanied by atlanta police department officers who were staged outside; the defendant is the UNITED STATES, sued under the federal tort claims act; the courts are the united states district court for the northern district of georgia, the united states court of appeals for the eleventh circuit, and the supreme court of the united states. therefore: never 'police raided', never 'atlanta police raided', never 'the state', never 'the city', never 'georgia', never 'cops', and never 'the government took' where what is meant is that the united states asserted immunity. every figure, name and outcome placed in a title or on a thumbnail must be locatable in EP70_wronghouse_script.en.v001.md or in EP70_wronghouse_FACTS_LEDGER.v001.md with the row cited, because config/ship_policy.v001.json puts title and thumbnail text in the blocking factual_support class and no mechanical check can detect a lie that is the right length and the right shape

NOT A DEVIATION, RECORDED SO IT IS NOT MISREAD AS ONE -- the episode number. notes: RUNTIME AND WORD BANDS ARE DERIVED, NOT CHOSEN. Pace basis is docs/PD_CANON.md rule 25: the measured end-to-end band is 159.5-169.7 wpm (EP66's delivered master is 4,278 words / 1604.211 s = 160.0 wpm). The narration tool's own printed 'measured wpm' counts speech only, excludes inter-chunk silence, is ~7% fast, and is NOT used. Finished film = narration master + ENDCARD_SEC 9.0, leadSeconds 0. R_lo = 60*6900/169.7 + 9.0 = 2439.6 + 9.0 = 2448.6 s (fewest words at the fastest measured pace); R_hi = 60*7500/159.5 + 9.0 = 2821.3 + 9.0 = 2830.3 s (most words at the slowest). The declared band [2445, 2835] contains both edges, so it holds across the whole measured range rather than at one assumed pace. At the design centre of 7,200 words the film lands 2700.0 s narration + 9.0 = 2709.0 s = 45:09. CUT BUDGET, checked so the contract is satisfiable (EP66 declared one that was not): at target_cut_sec 4.2 the film holds 582 cuts at the short edge, 645 at the design centre and 675 at the long edge; stills may occupy at most 32% of cuts, so still cuts are <= 186 / 206 / 216 and video cuts are >= 396 / 439 / 459. mandatory_stills 160 therefore fits inside the still ceiling at BOTH edges, and distinct_video_assets 300 fits inside the video budget at BOTH edges with 96 cuts of headroom at the short edge. SECTIONS: eight, not nine. The first draft declared ACT_6 and the script wrote a '## ACT_6' heading; gen_narration_case.section_for_heading knows HOOK / OP / ACT_1..ACT_5 / ENDING and nothing else, and extract_events DROPS prose under an unmapped heading, so 847 words -- the whole final movement -- were missing from the count the paid narration run is built from. It was caught by RUNNING the extractor, not by reading it. The fix is in the script, not in the shared tool: the sixth movement is headed '### ACT_5 - PART TWO' and maps to ACT_5. The extractor now returns 0 orphans and eight non-empty sections. That makes ACT_5 a double-length act (2,011 words against 863-1,327 for the others), which is why figure_beats_per_act tops out at 26 rather than 18: the floor of 12 still binds the short acts and the ceiling has to admit a twelve-minute act that carries THE MOMENT, THE SYSTEM MAP and THE HIDDEN RULE. The plate count is derived the EP69 way -- one commissioned plate per 45 narration words, section by section, with a floor of 8 for the HOOK and 2 for the OP -- which on a 7,200-word design centre gives 160. PRODUCIBILITY, measured 2026-08-12 and reproducible from episodes/_planning/measurements/EP71_wronghouse_registers.py against the same 26,101-clip pool EP68 and EP70 used: era-neutral registers (hands, paper, doors, mail, clocks, dawn, corridors, weather, files, texture, maps, screens) union 7,534 -> 0.053 GREEN at 400 cuts, and that is the real and reproducible strength of this shelf. The narrow core -- the frames that must read as a specific thing -- lands 0.380 AMBER on a tight regex and 0.437 RED on EP70's published three-bucket definition, and inside that core two registers fail outright rather than being merely thin: the 5 a.m. breach (one usable modern clip on the entire shelf) and April 1973 (at most three usable archival clips, none of them American). BOTH ARE COVERED BY NAMED PLATE-AND-I2V BUDGETS IN approved_deviations RATHER THAN BY MORE QUERYING, because more querying does not fix an absence. PEOPLE PLATES ARE THE 26 IDS NAMED ABOVE AND THEY ARE NOT A CONTIGUOUS BLOCK. The first draft declared W011-W036 as a block, which is the filename-does-not-carry-meaning failure EP62-65 hit from the other direction; the builder in 04_scenes/build_codex_order.v001.py refused to write until this list matched the plates that actually contain a person, and it also caught four plates that had been marked as people plates while depicting an empty car park, a doorframe, a sheet of chipboard and an office chair. Every one of the 26 is a hand, a forearm, a shoulder, a back, a pair of boots or a pair of shoes. There is not one face in this film. THE EMOTIONAL CENTRE OF THIS FILM MAY NOT BE SHOWN. A seven-year-old was under a blanket in the room across the hall and he is a real person who is now about sixteen; his mother was on a closet floor half-dressed with a rifle on her; her partner was reaching for a shotgun when the door opened. There is no depiction of any of them, no child anywhere in this film, no face of anyone real, and no generated document. What the film shows instead is fixed beat by beat in the binding substitution table in EP70_wronghouse_FILM_BIBLE.v001.md, and the forbidden_subjects list above is the machine half of that same decision.
